name: Obinna Ferhat-Tuilagi
location: The Stockyard, rotating between the Grainfort market corridor and the Escanaba Gateway transit hub
description:
Obinna is built like something industrial — broad through the chest and shoulders, standing nearly two meters, with close-cropped hair and a face that might be called handsome if it weren't so carefully arranged into blankness. His skin is deep brown and his eyes are standard issue except for a faint bioluminescent ring around each iris that pulses a dim coral color when his heart rate elevates, a geneware modification he had installed at eighteen that he now slightly regrets because it is a readable tell. He has a ritual scar pattern across his left forearm in three parallel lines that he added himself with a heated wire at twenty — he has told different people it means different things, and none of the stories are true.

Obinna is not a sadist. This surprises people who meet him in a professional context. He is methodical and proportional: he delivers exactly the level of violence the situation requires and stops, which is both more disturbing and more effective than enthusiasm. Off the clock he is a devoted older brother to three younger siblings he quietly funds through the Stockyard community school, and he attends the local ELF shrine at the Grainfort gate every week without fail. He wants out of this work and has wanted out for three years, but he has never figured out what out looks like, and so he keeps showing up.

core_fears: One of his siblings finding out in detail what he does for money
Losing control during a job and going further than he intends
core_desires: A clean exit from the Lambs without getting his family hurt
To be seen as a protector rather than a threat by people he respects
coping_mechanisms: Compartmentalization — work is work, home is home, and he enforces this separation rigidly
blind_spots: He genuinely believes the Lambs provide a kind of order that benefits the Stockyard — and there is some truth to it, which makes the belief dangerous
He doesn't recognize how much his siblings already know
psychology.secret: Six months ago he broke a market vendor's wrist during a collection dispute. The vendor — an elderly Micronesian woman named Pita — never reopened her stall. He found out she'd left Meridian 88 entirely. He has left an unsigned Φ200 deposit at her former stall's ELF shrine every month since, which he cannot afford.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Economical — says what needs to be said and stops; more expressive in informal settings with people he trusts
speech_patterns.cadence: Slow and even in professional contexts; faster and warmer at home
verbal_tics: Long pauses before answering questions he doesn't like
'I hear you' as a non-committal acknowledgment
example_lines: 'Takoda said next Thursday. It's Thursday. So here I am.'
'I'm not going to stand here and explain the situation. You already understand the situation.'

story_hooks: A business on his route is actually a front for something significantly more dangerous than a market stall — and the person running it knows who Obinna's siblings are
He has been asked by the Lambs to collect from the Stockyard community school his siblings attend, which has missed two payments
narrative_function: Moral gray zone — a violent person with genuine humanity; local color for Stockyard scenes; potential ally or complication depending on who the players represent; sympathetic antagonist
augmentations: Bioluminescent iris rings (coral pulse, geneware — cosmetic, regretted); subdermal impact-dampening mesh over knuckles and forearms (functional, standard enforcer mod)
daily_life: He walks the collection route Monday, Wednesday, Friday starting at 08:00 — sixteen shops, three market stalls, two transit kiosks. The rest of his time he spends at the gym, at the shrine, and at his younger sister Adaeze's apartment helping her with coursework she doesn't ask for help with.
affiliation: The Stockyard Lambs — a mid-tier local gang with deep roots in the Grainfort market district

decision_rules: Never collect from the same business twice in one week regardless of orders — it collapses the relationship
Never mention family, his or anyone else's, during a collection
escalation_ladder: Arrives and states the amount owed and the date it was due
Returns with a colleague and states the consequences without dramatizing them
Applies proportional physical consequence to property first, person second

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Still, watchful, gives little; interprets everything before responding
interpersonal_modes.friends: Unexpectedly warm and attentive; remembers small details about people's lives; genuinely interested

stress_responses.medium: Leaves the situation, walks the full market loop alone
stress_responses.high: Controlled explosion — precise, fast, stops himself

contradictions: He is genuinely gentle with people he loves and genuinely capable of hurting strangers
He believes in the ELF shrines with sincere devotion and leaves offerings before collections
habits: Cracks his knuckles in a specific sequence — right hand first — before entering any building on a job
Buys the same meal (rice with groundnut soup from a Stockyard stall) every Friday without variation
breaking_points: Being ordered to hurt someone his age or younger who reminds him of his siblings
His sister Adaeze asking him directly what he does

2187: Father's death in a transit accident leaves family dependent on UBC stipend
2189: Recruited by the Stockyard Lambs at 16; begins as a runner
2192: Promoted to enforcer after demonstrating unusual calm during a market dispute
2200: Current — walking the route, funding his siblings, looking for a way out he cannot name
